item.title: The Republican Party’s Financial Advantage Wasn’t Enough in the 2026 Midterm Elections
item.description: With the economy and national political climate of 2026: “You’re not going to advertise your way out of that,” said one expert.
item.dc:creator: Theodore Schleifer

media:content.media:credit: Tamir Kalifa for The New York Times
media:content.media:description: Supporters of Ken Paxton, the Texas Republican Senate candidate, watching the results at his election night watch party in Dallas on Tuesday.

item.title: What Makes These Election Results So Historic
item.description: Democrats celebrated a seismic triumph in the midterm elections, winning control of the Senate and the House as voters delivered a blistering rebuke to President Trump. Peter Baker, The New York Times’s Chief White House correspondent explains what this historic reset of the balance of power in Washington means.
item.dc:creator: Peter Baker, Alexandra Ostasiewicz, Nikolay Nikolov, Thomas Vollkommer, Rafaela Balster, James Surdam, Edward Vega and Rachel Buigas-Lopez

item.title: A Night of Firsts in the Midterms
item.description: The midterms were full of firsts, including the first Black woman to be elected governor of a U.S. state and the first openly gay man to serve in the Senate.
item.dc:creator: Monika Cvorak

media:content.media:credit: Reba Saldanha/Associated Press; Nicole Craine for The New York Times

item.title: There’s No Modern Precedent for This Democratic Tsunami
item.description: It was hard to imagine that an electoral wave this big was still possible. But there have been extraordinary changes just beneath the surface.
item.dc:creator: Nate Cohn

item.title: My Adult Daughter Has Gone ‘No Contact’ With Me. What Should I Do?
item.description: A mother is distraught to find herself cut out of her daughter’s life after a frustrated outburst. Family therapy? Her daughter says no thanks.
item.dc:creator: Philip Galanes

item.title: America’s Trade Deficit Remained Elevated in September
item.description: The gap between U.S. exports and imports, which remained at a relatively high level in September, has defied efforts by President Trump to decrease it with tariffs.
item.dc:creator: Ana Swanson

item.title: El-Sayed Wins Michigan Senate Race
item.description: Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, a progressive Democrat and outspoken critic of Israel, won Michigan’s Senate race, maintaining his party’s hold on a crucial battleground seat and becoming the nation’s first Muslim senator.
item.dc:creator: Gaia Lamperti

media:content.media:description: Dr. Abdul El-Sayed defeated former Representative Mike Rogers, a Republican, in a race that focused heavily on the politics of Israel.

item.title: The Business Fallout From a Blue Wave
item.description: Investors are already picking the winners and the losers after Democrats glided to a landslide victory in the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Ross Sorkin, Bernhard Warner, Sarah Kessler, Michael J. de la Merced, Niko Gallogly, Brian O’Keefe, Sri Muppidi and Ian Mount
item.category: House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform

media:content.media:description: Voters delivered a landslide victory that looks set to redraw the American political map.

item.title: Black Candidates for Governor Break Barriers in Four States
item.description: Georgia was the first state to elect a female Black governor with Keisha Lance Bottoms. Three other states elected Black governors for the first time.
item.dc:creator: Emily Cochrane

item.title: Democrats Deliver a Big Blue Bludgeoning
item.description: The party’s midterm victory reshapes the political landscape.
item.dc:creator: Jess Bidgood

media:content.media:description: Supporters celebrating at James Talarico’s watch party.

item.title: Israel’s President Will Start Talks on Whether Netanyahu or Eisenkot Can Form a Government
item.description: President Isaac Herzog will meet with party leaders over the next two days to decide whether to give Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu or rivals the first chance at forming a coalition.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Boxerman

media:content.media:description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog delivers remarks at his official residence in Jerusalem on Monday.

item.title: The New York Times Adds 420,000 Digital Subscribers
item.description: The additions in the third quarter keep the company roughly on track to meet its goal of 15 million subscribers by the end of next year, after a slower second quarter.
item.dc:creator: Katie Robertson

media:content.media:credit: Lucia Vazquez for The New York Times
media:content.media:description: The New York Times Company has added about 1.46 million digital-only subscribers over the past year.

item.title: CVS to Split Off Pharmacy Business, Ending the Healthcare Conglomerate Era
item.description: In a breakup planned for 2028, CVS Health intends to split off its pharmacies into a new company, while keeping together its businesses in insurance and pharmacy benefits.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Robbins

media:content.media:credit: Philip Cheung for The New York Times

item.title: The 7 Senate Flips That Ended Decades of Republican Control
item.description: Democrats flipped several Senate seats, most of which had been held by Republicans since former President Obama was elected in 2008.
item.dc:creator: Albert Sun, Minho Kim, Marco Hernandez and Emily Davies

item.title: A Blue Wave
item.description: In a rebuke to President Trump, the Democrats flipped both the Senate and the House.
item.dc:creator: Sam Sifton

media:content.media:credit: Nicole Craine for The New York Times
media:content.media:description: A celebration of Senator Jon Ossoff’s re-election in Georgia.

item.title: Musk Faces Setback as SpaceX and Tesla Stocks Tumble on Midterm Election Results
item.description: The world’s richest person has antagonized Democrats, some of whom have signaled their intent to investigate him when they take control of Congress.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Mac

media:content.media:description: SpaceX and Tesla are based in Texas, where voters elected a Democratic senator and governor.

item.title: How Astronauts Voted From Space in the Midterm Elections
item.description: Americans voted absentee from the International Space Station, Antarctica and remote Alaskan villages.
item.dc:creator: Yan Zhuang
